checks.meanings: `audible` correctly covers basic hearability; `clear` correctly covers speech that is easy to hear and understand
checks.usage: `Am I audible?`, `Am I clear?` and contextual `You are clear.` are grammatical and coherent in the stated telephone sound-check setting
checks.qualification: The text distinguishes hearability from clarity without falsely claiming that `clear` can never concern audibility
checks.phoneticBanks: `audible/edible/laudable` and `clear/near/fear` are real, non-homophonous near-sound sets; the feedback uses stable initial-vowel or initial-consonant cues
checks.sceneAndAnswers: coherent and unambiguous across all 17 tasks
